updates.title: Long-running agent reliability is becoming the real bottleneck
updates.whatChanged: Frontier agent systems can already execute multi-step work, but reliability falls as tasks get longer and tool use becomes more complex. The industry is increasingly focusing on state, recovery, verification and trajectory-level control rather than only model quality.
updates.whyCare: For enterprise architecture, the important question is shifting from whether an agent can do one task to whether it can complete a long workflow safely and repeatedly.
updates.before: Agents were judged mainly on impressive individual tasks and demos.
updates.after: Architecture increasingly centers on reliable execution across many steps, tools, failures and approvals.
updates.learn: Long-horizon reliability, persistent state, retries, recovery, verification and human escalation.

updates.title: Agent security is moving from app security to actor-level control
updates.whatChanged: As agents gain tools and autonomy, enterprises increasingly need agent identity, scoped permissions, sandboxing, audit logs and approval gates.
updates.whyCare: An agent with access to enterprise systems behaves more like a software actor than a chatbot. It needs its own operating controls.
updates.before: Secure the AI application and its API access.
updates.after: Secure each agent as an actor with identity, privileges and auditable actions.
updates.learn: Least privilege, credential isolation, agent identity, sandboxing and approval gates.

updates.title: Managed agent runtimes reduce custom harness work
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced a managed agent runtime that packages context, tools, subagents, execution and long-running task infrastructure.
updates.whyCare: The underlying pattern was already available through custom stacks and other frameworks. The meaningful change is lower implementation friction for teams using that provider.
updates.before: Teams assembled much of the harness themselves or through separate frameworks.
updates.after: More runtime pieces can be consumed as managed infrastructure.
updates.learn: Agent harness = state, context, tools, execution, retries, permissions, memory and observability.

updates.title: Agent evaluation is expanding from output quality to behaviour
updates.whatChanged: Teams increasingly need to inspect what tools an agent used, which path it took, and whether it stayed inside policy, not only whether the final answer looked correct.
updates.whyCare: A correct-looking output can still come from an unsafe or invalid path. That matters once agents can take actions.
updates.before: Evaluate whether the final answer is correct.
updates.after: Evaluate both the result and the action trajectory that produced it.
updates.learn: Output evals, trajectory evals, audit logs, policy checks and risk-based human review.
